Bench: Gautam Kumar Choudhary  Cr. Appeal (S.J.) No. 226 of 2013

(Against the judgment of conviction dated 18.03.2013 and order of sentence dated  19.03.2013 passed by learned 1st Assistant Sessions Judge, Hazaribagh in S.T. No.
 271 of 2004)
 -----
 Md. Wasiuddin ... .... Appellant  Versus  The State of Jharkhand ... .... Respondent  PR ES ENT CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE GAUTAM KUMAR CHOUDHARY -----
For the Appellant : Mr. Rajendra Pd. Gupta, Advocate For the State : Mr. Someshwar Roy, APP -----
By Court :
Heard the parties 1. The judgment of conviction and order of sentence under Section 304B of Indian Penal Code is under challenge in the instant appeal.
2. The appellant happened to be the brother-in-law (Devar) of the deceased.

As per fardbeyan of the deceased Jahida Parveen @ Nilu, which was recorded on 25.11.1997 at 9 O'clock in the morning at Sadar Hospital, Hazaribagh by Asstt.
Sub Inspector Lalan Ram, she was married to Gulam Sarwar six month before the incidence.
After the marriage, she resumed her marital life in her matrimonial home and her husband after two months moved to Delhi to earn his livelihood.

It is alleged that after her husband went away, her mother-in-law and brother-in-law- Md. Wasiuddin started making allegation that her father had given less dowry in comparison to his another daughter, and a demand of Rs. 15,000/- was made.
She was abused and assaulted by them in reference to dowry demand.
When she sent message to her father about her harassment, he came there and tried to resolve the matter with her family members but one month after they again started harassing for dowry demand.

It is alleged that in the morning Md. Wasiuddin vs The State Of Jharkhand on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130907384/

sentences.text: while she was sleeping, she was set on fire as a result, she sustained critical burn injury.
After the incidence, she was taken to the hospital by her uncle-in-law and mother-in-law.

3. On the basis of statement of the deceased, Hazaribagh Sadar PS Case No. 423 of 1997 was registered under Sections 498A, 324, 307/34 of the Indian Penal Code against the mother-in-law and brother-in-law on 25.11.1997.
4. Police on investigation found the case true and submitted charge sheet against both of them.
After cognizance, charge was framed and the accused were put on trial for the offence under Sections 498A and 304B of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3/ 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
During course of trial, Jahida Parveen @ Nilu died.

5. Altogether 13 witnesses were examined on behalf of the prosecution and the relevant documents,
including the fardbeyan and postmortem examination report, were adduced into evidence, marked as exhibits.
After prosecution evidence, the statement of the accused has been recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
The defence is of innocence and false implication.

6. Judgment of conviction and order of sentence has been assailed on the ground that three independent witnesses i.e. PWs 7, 8, 10 and 11 have been turned hostile and not supported the prosecution case.
PWs 4 and 5 were the compounders and both of them were present in the hospital at the relevant time.
They have deposed that the death was accidental in nature caused by fire of lamp.
The appellant has served sentenced for almost 15 months.
7. Learned counsel for the State has defended the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence.

It is submitted that bare perusal of the statement of witnesses will show that during progress of trial none of the witnesses have been given suggestion in the cross-examination that it was a case of accidental death caused by burning lamp.
Death took place only after six months of the marriage and there was evidence of dowry demand being made from the deceased by this appellant.
On these evidence a presumption under Section 113 B is liable to drawn that the appellant cause dowry death of the deceased.
Fardbeyan is to be treated as a dying declaration as after her statement was recorded the deceased died during course of treatment due to burn injury.
At no point of time defence was taken that death was accidental in nature.

8. After having considered the submissions advanced on behalf of both sides and the materials on record, there cannot be any doubt regarding the cause of death of the deceased by burn injury as deposed to by the Doctor (PW-3).
It is also not in dispute that the death took place within seven years of marriage.

9. With regard to dowry demand the deceased in her statement to the police as is stated that she was subjected to harassment in reference to dowry demand by this appellant and also by her mother-in-law (died during trial).

This being her last statement with regard to the cause of death can be treated as dying declaration which is a substantive piece of evidence and on its basis and judgment of conviction can be returned, if it is reliable and trustworthy.
Her, testimony is duly corroborated by PW1, PW2 and PW3.

sentences.text: In this view of matter prosecution case cannot be thrown out merely on the testimony of PW4 and PW5 that the deceased had told them that death was accidental in nature.

Had it been a case of accidental death by burning with the lamp, then in such circumstance it was incumbent on the part of the defence to have taken it at the very initial stage while giving suggestions to the witnesses.
No such suggestion has been given from which an inference can be drawn that deceased had died an accidental death.
This court is of the view that reliance can be placed on the dying declaration of the deceased, which is corroborated by other evidence.
For the reasons as discussed above, I do not find any infirmity in the judgment of conviction and order of sentence which is accordingly upheld.
The Appeal is dismissed.
The appellant's bail is cancelled.
He is directed to surrender before the court below within two weeks to serve the remaining part of sentence.

(Gautam Kumar Choudhary, J.) Jharkhand High Court, Ranchi Dated, the 12th April, 2024 NAFR/
